findings.title: Potential SQL injection
findings.message: Supported user input reaches a SQL query argument; use bound query parameters.

findings.title: React dangerouslySetInnerHTML usage
findings.message: Review React dangerouslySetInnerHTML usage and sanitize untrusted HTML before rendering.

limitations: Static source evidence only; never a complete runtime import or call graph.
No target code, dependency installation, LLM, import hooks, or external API is executed.
Host Python grammar/stdlib and configured file, byte, entry and AST limits bound coverage.
Source-root candidates are conservative; runtime sys.path and packaging hooks are not evaluated.
Unknown external modules, dynamic imports/attributes, re-exports and wildcard symbols can remain unresolved.
Filename classifications are inferred; framework declarations do not prove runtime use or authentication coverage.
Literal defaults, annotation strings, route paths, arguments, assignment values and docstrings are omitted.
The caller must own a stable repository and prevent concurrent filesystem replacement.
Edges represent resolved file-backed static imports: importer -> imported module, not runtime calls.
Unknown, ambiguous, namespace-only, external and stdlib imports do not create internal edges.
Unparsed modules and unresolved imports can hide dependencies; isolation and metrics concern only observed edges.
Confirmed roles mean explicit static evidence; inferred roles are naming heuristics, not enforced layers.
Cycles are detected by strongly connected components with one witness each; not every simple cycle is enumerated.
Graph metrics alone do not establish architecture quality, exploitability or vulnerability impact.
Static Python/configuration indicators only; no exploitability or comprehensive compliance claim.
The caller must supply a trusted scanner result for the same stable repository version; no cross-run identity is inferred.
No uploaded code, dependencies, image build, network call, LLM, or additional security scan runs inside the checklist evaluator.
PASS is limited to the described indicator or local rule scope; zero findings does not establish security.
UTF-8, host Python grammar, bounded inventory, and generated-directory exclusions limit coverage.
Source values, environment values, raw scanner messages and raw dependency URLs are never copied to checklist output.

checks.title: Hardcoded credential patterns
checks.description: No supported hardcoded credential pattern in the supplied complete scan.
checks.remediation: Load secrets from a managed secret store or environment and rotate exposed credentials.
limitations: Only credential-like names and literal patterns supported by the local rule pack are covered.

checks.title: Environment configuration indicator
checks.description: Observe static environment-based configuration access; this is not proof that all config is externalized.
checks.remediation: Use deploy-time environment configuration instead of hardcoding deploy-specific values.
limitations: An environment read is an indicator only; runtime settings and secret-store access are not verified.

checks.title: Sensitive filenames and ignore policy
checks.description: Inspect sensitive-named files and a bounded subset of root gitignore patterns.
checks.remediation: Exclude local secrets/private keys from version control; inspect tracking history and rotate any exposed values.
limitations: No Git index/history inspection. Ignored sensitive files still require review; public certificate files may match names.

checks.title: Explicit production debug settings
checks.description: Check supported Flask scan findings and explicit FastAPI/Django debug indicators.
checks.remediation: Disable development debug mode in deployed applications and verify effective environment settings.
limitations: No runtime or deployment environment is inferred; dynamic settings require review.

checks.title: Explicit TLS verification flags
checks.remediation: Enable certificate verification and use a trusted CA bundle.
limitations: Only requests/httpx/ssl patterns in the local pack are covered; custom transports are not modeled.

checks.title: Modeled SQL injection flows
checks.description: Check supported input-to-query flows, preserving existing Semgrep evidence.
checks.remediation: Bind values separately from constant SQL using the database driver parameter API.
limitations: OSS taint scope and modeled input sources only; no database runtime or universal query analysis.

checks.title: Modeled shell and dynamic execution risks
checks.description: Check supported shell input flows and dynamic eval/exec findings.
checks.remediation: Use fixed executables and argument arrays without shell interpretation; avoid dynamic Python execution.
limitations: No general shell=False argument-injection proof; supported taint sources and API names only.

checks.title: Supported password hash patterns
checks.description: Check fast hashing of password-named input in supported hashlib constructors.
checks.remediation: Use a salted password KDF with an appropriate work factor.
limitations: Naming-based indicators do not establish complete authentication or password-storage coverage.

checks.title: Modeled unsafe deserialization
checks.description: Check supported untrusted pickle flows and unsafe PyYAML loader patterns.
reference_categories: A08:2021 - Software and Data Integrity Failures
checks.remediation: Use data-only formats and safe YAML loaders for untrusted input.
limitations: Unmodeled inputs and custom serializers remain unassessed even with zero findings.

checks.title: Static CORS configuration
checks.description: Inspect explicit origins and credentials on recognized FastAPI/Starlette and Flask-CORS APIs.
checks.remediation: Use a reviewed explicit origin allowlist; do not combine wildcard origins and credentials.
limitations: Wildcard public APIs need policy review; explicit allowlists are configuration indicators, not an authorization proof.

checks.title: Authentication coverage indicators
checks.description: Locate authentication imports/decorators without claiming route protection.
checks.remediation: Review access policy and verify protected routes and object-level authorization with dedicated tests.
limitations: Authentication decorators/imports never prove coverage. This check cannot return PASS from static indicators.

checks.title: Python dependency manifest presence
checks.description: Check for requirements files, pyproject.toml, Pipfile, setup.py or setup.cfg.
checks.remediation: Declare dependencies in a supported version-controlled manifest.
limitations: Presence only; setup.py is never executed, and dependencies are never installed.

checks.title: Dependency version declaration bounds
checks.description: Inspect requirements and PEP 621/build-system dependency specifiers.
checks.remediation: Pin application dependencies or use reviewed bounded compatible ranges and a maintained lock strategy.
limitations: No vulnerability, resolution, compatibility or supply-chain audit. Includes, direct URLs and unparsed formats require review.

checks.title: Python test filename indicator
checks.description: Check for test_*.py or *_test.py filenames without executing them.
checks.remediation: Maintain and run security-relevant tests in a trusted development pipeline.
limitations: Names indicate presence only, not test quality, passing status or exercised security coverage.

checks.title: Docker final-stage user declaration
checks.description: Inspect an explicit USER declaration in the final Dockerfile stage.
checks.remediation: Declare an appropriate non-root runtime user in the final image and verify its effective UID.
limitations: No image is built or inspected. Base-image defaults, named UID mappings and inherited stage users are not resolved.
Static import reachability indicates potential relevance, not confirmed exploit propagation or runtime calls.
Severity and CWE belong only to the original finding; dependent modules are not assigned that vulnerability.
The caller must supply scan, structure and graph from the same immutable repository version.
Cross-input references are checked, but these existing contracts do not prove repository snapshot identity.
Unknown, ambiguous, conditional, dynamic and omitted external dependencies limit coverage.
Only bounded shortest observed import paths are returned; longer alternate paths are not enumerated.
Unparsed source cannot be mapped to a trusted symbol; unmapped findings remain explicit.
Source text, finding title/message, literal values and raw diagnostics are omitted from this evidence package.

prohibited_dependencies.reason: Data-access modules must not depend on HTTP controller modules.

limitations: Architecture observations are static structural indicators and heuristic guidelines, not runtime defects or security vulnerabilities.
Edges reflect observed static internal imports only; dynamic imports, reflection, runtime hooks and unknown external dependencies are not fully captured.
Inferred module roles rely on filename/path heuristics rather than confirmed framework or database bindings.
Size, coupling, inheritance and responsibility thresholds are configurable heuristics and do not produce an overall architecture quality score.
Recommendations are advisory, context-dependent and require human engineering review; source files are never automatically rewritten.
No runtime latency, throughput, scalability improvement or exploitability probability is claimed without runtime measurement.
